title: HE WEPT OVER HIM AND KISSED HIM

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Joseph threw himself on his father and wept over him and kissed him." — Gen 50:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Genesis has shown us Joseph as a dreaming boy, a slave, a prisoner, and the second most powerful man in Egypt. Here it shows us a son.

He throws himself on his father's body and weeps. All the composure of a ruler is gone. There is no protocol in this, no dignity being maintained. Just a grown man crying over the father he has lost.

We sometimes imagine that spiritual maturity means grieving quietly, or quickly, or with more visible faith. Scripture disagrees. Abraham mourned Sarah. David wept for Absalom. Jesus stood at Lazarus's grave and wept, knowing full well He was about to raise him (Jn 11:35).

Grief is not a failure of faith. It is love with nowhere left to go.

Paul told the Thessalonians not to grieve like those who have no hope (1 Thess 4:13). Notice what he did not say. He did not say "do not grieve." Christians grieve — deeply, honestly, sometimes for years. We simply grieve differently, because we know the story is not over.

If you have lost someone, you have permission to weep. The One who wept at a graveside understands exactly.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you allowed yourself to grieve honestly, or tried to be strong too quickly?
2. What does it mean to grieve with hope rather than without it?
3. Who around you is grieving and needs someone simply to sit with them?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You do not ask me to hide my grief. Meet me in my sorrow, and hold me with the hope that in Christ death does not have the last word. Amen.
